events.summary: Sri Lanka launched its five-year National Anti-Corruption Action Plan.
Officials were directed to prepare action plans and report implementation progress.
Opposition leader proposed a ten-point plan to reduce elephant-human conflict.
July elderly allowances were credited for 600,768 Aswesuma beneficiaries.
Minister opened a temporary women's shelter in Nuwara Eliya.
Cabinet approved signing an agreement for seasonal E-8 employment opportunities in South Korea.
Ministry implemented upper-secondary vocational education with NVQ Level 4 pathways.
Railways announced special services for the Kandy Esala Perahera.
GovPay traffic-fine payments began in Western Province and expressways
Authorities planned to provide 1,000 phones to traffic police officers
Education reforms proposed revised school hours and two daily breaks
Health ministry planned 2,000 primary health centres nationwide within three years
Sri Lanka plans broad ground-penetrating radar scans at the Semmani mass grave.
Public Security Ministry plans to recruit 10,000 civil defence officers into police service.
IAEA confirms five potential sites identified for Sri Lanka’s first nuclear power plant.
Sri Lanka’s Cabinet approved the nuclear power initiative.
Sri Lanka created a nuclear power project implementation organisation.
Health Ministry initiated a special programme to improve Batticaloa health services.
Sri Lanka and France signed a bilateral debt restructuring agreement.
Sri Lanka, France and French agencies signed debt restructuring implementation letters.
Government proposed establishing a council for national industrial planning.
Prime Minister launched the RDB Quick App online banking service.
Authorities decided to protect archaeological sites while releasing vacant land.
President ordered rapid recruitment of 5,000 civil defence assistants for elephant-conflict response.
Officials opened one Upper Kotmale Reservoir spillway gate after heavy rainfall.
President proposed closing, merging, and creating schools according to local needs.
CPC agreed with distributors to implement a fuel distribution cost-management plan.
Government announced module-based education reforms for implementation from 2026.
President appointed a committee to investigate alleged SriLankan Airlines corruption and irregularities.
Treasury funds had been allocated to procure medicines for hospitals.
Passenger ferry service between Sri Lanka and India began operations on 14 October 2023.
Minister ordered a study on starting luxury air-conditioned bus services in Mullaitivu.
Cabinet approved establishing a cyber threat and malware analysis research unit.
Cabinet approved signing an AI cooperation memorandum with Singapore's National University.
President instructed officials to ensure continuous medicine procurement and distribution without shortages.
Welfare Benefits Board extended the deadline for Aswesuma phase two appeals and objections.
A physiotherapy unit opened at Thirukkovil Base Hospital with the chairman’s financial contribution.
A second-phase hospital development allocation of approximately LKR 3 million was announced.
The government decided to extend school hours by thirty minutes under education reforms.
Minister expects electronic national identity cards to be issued by April 2026.
India-supported media training workshop was conducted in Jaffna.
Alumni association donated infusion pumps and a multiparameter monitor to Apeksha Hospital.
India will fund homes for 4,700 hill-country families.
Sri Lanka will fund basic facilities for 4,700 homes.
Fifty resettlement houses have been completed for landslide victims.
Authorities opened one spillway gate at Upper Kotmale Reservoir.
Government will begin training teacher trainees nationwide from August.
District committee decided to use government-controlled land for cultivation.
Aswesuma appeals deadline ends on July 21, with 30,000 appeals received.
Six rehabilitated elephants were released into Udawalawe National Park.
President opened a Rs. 300 million wax museum at the historic Ehelebpola Walawwa.
China donated Sri Lanka’s full 2025 school uniform requirement.
Kandy schools were ordered closed during the Esala Perahera period.
Energy minister expects 2,000 MW of solar power generation within five years.
Health ministry plans 1,990 new appointments to the health service.
Police headquarters opened a subsidized salon for officers and their families.
